bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : CM Samrat Choudhary urges assistant professors to ensure 75% attendance in colleges
bihar_raw_news.content: Higher Education 2 min read Bihar: CM Samrat Choudhary urges assistant professors to ensure 75% attendance in colleges Addressing a gathering of newly appointed assistant professors, CM Choudhary said the state government had opened 211 degree colleges and appointed 2,451 assistant professors, describing the expansion of higher education infrastructure as a major achievement. ANI Published On Sep 13, 2026 at 07:34 PM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bihar: CM Samrat Choudhary urges assistant professors to ensure 75% attendance in colleges New Delhi : Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has urged newly appointed assistant professors to ensure at least 75 per cent attendance of students in colleges, saying the government's efforts to expand higher education would not yield results if students did not attend classes regularly. Addressing a gathering of newly appointed assistant professors, CM Choudhary said the state government had opened 211 degree colleges and appointed 2,451 assistant professors, describing the expansion of higher education infrastructure as a major achievement. Advt He said the newly appointed teachers would play a key role in strengthening the academic ecosystem of the new colleges, particularly those located in rural areas and ensuring that students make full use of the facilities being created by the government. "Until children come and study in your colleges, the importance of that college will not be realised. Ensure that 75 per cent of students attend your college under all circumstances so that you can teach them," CM Choudhary said. He said students from Bihar were still travelling to cities such as Kota, Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru for higher education and competitive examination preparation. Citing examples of students studying outside the state, the Chief Minister said around 11,000 students from Bihar were studying at Lovely Professional University, while another institute in had more than 40,000 students from Bihar. "Today, around 8 to 10 lakh children from Bihar are still going outside the state to study," he said, adding that the expansion of degree colleges would provide students an opportunity to pursue higher education closer to their homes. CM Choudhary also said the government would identify 10 good international institutions and facilitate direct interaction between Bihar's teachers and those institutions. Advt He suggested that 100 teachers be identified and sent abroad for one-month courses to expose them to international standards of education. "One era saw us compromise quality with quantity. Now we have to take quality and quantity together," he said. The Chief Minister said the government would build college infrastructure, but the future of the institutions would depend on teachers and their efforts to improve the quality of education. He said Bihar spends more than 21 per cent of its budget in the education sector, covering primary schools, middle schools, high schools and colleges. CM Choudhary also highlighted the government's efforts to reduce the need for students to travel outside Bihar for education and said the state must compete

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to send 100 professors to Oxford and other global institutions for training
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar is set to take a major step towards improving the quality of higher education, with Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announcing an initiative to send 100 professors for training to Oxford and other prestigious institutions across the world. Samrat Choudhary said on Sunday that improving the quality of education also requires developing the capabilities of teachers and others associated with the education sector. As part of this effort, 100 professors will be identified and sent for training to Oxford and other reputed institutions worldwide. Opportunities will also be provided for interaction and experience-sharing with teachers and experts from some of the world’s leading educational institutions. Advertisement The Chief Minister was speaking while inaugurating the orientation programme for 2,451 newly appointed assistant professors in the state’s 211 newly established degree colleges. He said the Bihar government was giving the highest priority to education, with 21 per cent of the state’s total budget being spent on the education sector. Advertisement Choudhary said the government’s objective was not merely to increase the number of educational institutions, but to develop an education system in Bihar that is modern, high-quality and beneficial for the future of students. “Bihar has become the first state in the country to start 211 degree colleges in a single day. In the coming days, the state’s education system and academic infrastructure will be expanded on a large scale so that more students can access better facilities for higher education. The real purpose of establishing higher education institutions would be achieved only when students regularly attend colleges, interact with teachers and make use of the available academic resources,” he said. Choudhary said there was no shortage of talent among Bihar’s youth and that what was needed was access to quality education, modern resources and proper guidance. The newly appointed assistant professors, he said, could play an important role in this direction. “You have come forward to take Bihar’s education standards and its future ahead,” the Chief Minister told the newly appointed assistant professors, adding that quality education combined with extensive expansion of academic infrastructure would provide a new direction to the future of Bihar’s youth. bihar_raw_news.content: DA news: Full list of states that have announced dearness allowance hikes, payment of arrears for employees so far Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Sikkim, West Bengal and more — Check full list of states that have announced DA hikes so far, besides payment of DA arrears for employees and pensioners. Jocelyn Fernandes Published 13 Sep 2026, 05:41 PM IST Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Sikkim, West Bengal and other states have announced DA hikes and payment of DA arrears for employees and pensioners. ( AI generated image for representational purposes only ) AI Quick Read Updated biannually using data from the All-India Consumer Price Index (AICPI), dearness allowance (DA) is a percentage of employees' basic pay that aims to mitigate the inflation impact and rising cost of living. New announcements usually come in March and October, with rollouts in January and July. The last hike was announced in April this year, when the Finance Ministry increased DA from 58% to 60% of basic salary, effective from 1 January 2026. Over 1 crore beneficiaries, comprising some 50 lakh central government employees and about 65 lakh pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees, gain from an increase in DA and Dearness Relief (DR), respectively. It hiked basic salaries between ₹ 48,000 to ₹ 1,17,000 and DA from ₹ 435 to ₹ 1,050. Later, the Indian Railways also announced a 2% hike in DA and DR for staff and pensioners. Here's a look at the full list of DA hikes announced by states so far: Andhra Pradesh this month approved two long-pending DA revisions — giving a combined of 4.55% DA hike for state government employees, local body personnel and university staff. It will be implemented from September 2026 and disbursed with salary released in October this year. The first installment of 2.73% hike, which takes DA from 37.31% to 40.04% of basic pay comes retroactively in effect from July 2024; and the second installment of 1.82%, takes DA from 40.04% to 41.86% of basic pay comes retroactively in effect from January 2025. The arrears will be released in structured installments in 2027 and 2028 salaries. Arunachal Pradesh hiked DA and DR for its employees by 2%, effective from 1 January 2026. DA in basic pay is now up to 60% from 58% and will be implemented for 69,248 regular employees. bihar_raw_news.title: "Quality education, academic expansion will give new direction to Bihar's youth": Bihar CM
bihar_raw_news.content: "Quality education, academic expansion will give new direction to Bihar's youth": Bihar CM ANI | Updated: Sep 13, 2026 14:44 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 13 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday inaugurated the orientation programme for 2,451 newly appointed assistant professors across 211 newly created degree colleges in the state by lighting the ceremonial lamp at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna, according to the Chief Minister's Office. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister congratulated the newly appointed assistant professors and urged them to work with complete dedication, stating that they carry the vital responsibility of strengthening Bihar's education system and shaping the future of the upcoming generation. He noted that the role of teachers is not limited to imparting subject knowledge, but also extends to building the personality, mindset, and future of students, adding that quality education and extensive academic expansion will provide a new direction to the youth of Bihar. The Chief Minister said that Bihar has been a land of knowledge since ancient times, with great learning traditions like Nalanda and Vikramshila showing the path of wisdom to the entire world. He emphasised the need for Bihar to carry forward this glorious tradition with modern technology, quality education, and better academic facilities. Highlighting the state's focus on educational infrastructure, he stated that Bihar has become the first state in the country to start 211 degree colleges in a single day, adding that the state's educational structure will be expanded further in the coming days to provide higher education facilities to more students. Choudhary further announced that to strengthen school education, 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan model schools are being developed in the state. These schools will provide students with a better academic environment alongside coaching for competitive exams such as NEET and JEE, live classes, and 24x7 online tutor facilities to offer better opportunities for competitive exam preparation. Directing the newly appointed assistant professors to ensure that students attend college regularly and participate actively in classes, the Chief Minister said that merely increasing the number of colleges is not enough. He stressed that the true objective of establishing higher education institutions will be fulfilled only when students attend college regularly, interact with teachers, and utilise the available academic resources. He said that capacity building of teachers and education stakeholders is essential to improve the quality of education. To this end, an initiative will be undertaken to identify 100 professors and send them for training to world-renowned institutions, including Oxford. Opportunities will also be provided to interact and share experiences with educators and experts from top global institutions. He highlighted that the Bihar government has accorded top priority to education, allocating 21 per cent of the state's total budget to the sector, with the goal of creating an education system that is modern, quality-driven, and beneficial for students' futures. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Nearly 48 lakh affected by floods in 15 districts - Scroll.in
bihar_raw_news.content: Work to secure embankments at Rangra, Bhagalpur. | Water Resources Department, Government of Bihar, @WRD_Bihar/X The flood situation in Bihar worsened on Saturday, with the number of affected persons rising to nearly 48 lakh across 15 districts, reported PTI. With several rivers flowing above the danger mark, the Water Resources Department has cautioned against sudden and rapid riverbank erosion. Officials have been directed to monitor the situation and ensure any incident of erosion is reported promptly. The districts that are affected by the floods are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnia, Madhepura and Araria. Approximately 47.9 lakh persons have been affected in 575 gram panchayats across 87 blocks of the districts. The count of affected persons was 47.3 lakh on Friday evening. The state has received 104.1 mm of rainfall in September, about 27% above normal, PTI quoted unidentified officials as saying. This, coupled with rainfall in the catchment areas of Nepal, has caused several streams and rivers to swell. At 6 am on Saturday, the Ganga river at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur was flowing at 36.4 metres, 1.9 metres above the danger level, said the disaster management department. The water resources department said that rivers Gandak at Dumariaghat, Kosi at Baltara and Kursela, Burhi Gandak at Khagaria, Ganga at Digha, Gandhi Ghat, Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon and Munger, Punpun at Sripalpur, Bagmati at Benibad, and Ghaghra at Darauli and Gangpur Siswan were flowing above the danger marks. Most parts of Bihar are likely to remain partly cloudy on Sunday and Monday, with the possibility of strong winds, the Bihar Meteorological Centre has said. Edited by Sneha. national_raw_news.title: 21 mins ago | National 20 PM Modi holds 15 bilateral meetings with world leaders, besides engagements with heads of interna...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a series of high-level bilateral engagements on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Over the past three days, Mr Modi held 15 meetings with heads of state and government, besides several pull-aside meetings with world leaders and heads of international institutions. The meetings provided an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties, discuss issues of mutual interest and exchange views on regional and global developments. The Prime Minister today held bilateral talks with leaders of Kazakhstan, Egypt, Indonesia and Philippines, South Africa, Burundi, Nigeria and Uganda. The Prime Minister met President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The two leaders reviewed cooperation in a range of areas, including politics, trade, defence and security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals, emerging technologies, the creative economy and people-to-people ties. The Prime Minister also held a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. Mr. Modi also held talks with Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. He welcomed the Philippines’ decision to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. During his meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Mr. Modi reviewed the full range of the India-South Africa Strategic Partnership. Mr. Modi also met Nigerian Vice President Kashim Shettima. Yesterday, Mr Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders from Ethiopia, Malaysia, UAE, Vietnam and China. On Friday, the Prime Minister met leaders from Russia and Iran and also UN Secretary General.

national_raw_news.title: Lab-Grown Diamonds Offer Monumental Opportunity for India: Amit Shah 5 hours ago 54
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah today called upon the Indian gems and jewellery industry to ensure that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing chain of lab-grown diamonds remain firmly in Indian hands. Addressing the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai, Mr. Shah said the nature of the diamond trade is changing with the emergence of lab-grown diamonds. He said the lab-grown diamond market, in terms of volume, is expected to become nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market, describing it as a monumental opportunity for India. The Minister said India has the infrastructure, capabilities, capital and entrepreneurial talent needed to seize this opportunity. He urged the industry to build capabilities across the entire value chain, including manufacturing machinery, diamond production, jewellery making, branding and setting up showrooms of Indian companies in cities across the world. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event. Earlier in the day, Home Minister inaugurated a specially curated exhibition of manuscripts titled “Shri Ganesh Dnyanarati” at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Shah said India has a rich and vibrant knowledge tradition whose light has the potential to guide the entire world. He said this enduring legacy of knowledge has enabled the country to preserve its identity and civilisational continuity despite centuries of foreign invasions. Mr. Shah said the spirit of Bharat could never be enslaved because its memory remained alive in its history, language, culture, archives and traditions. He urged the Asiatic Society to use modern technology to take its vast repository of knowledge to people across the country. The Union Minister also visited the library and inspected the work being carried out at the Society’s manuscript conservation laboratory. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event.
